findings.title: Uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: The new token-refresh block in getClient calls `await prisma.credential.update({...})` but the module never imports `prisma` (imports are jsforce, rrule, zod, getLocation, WEBAPP_URL, HttpError, logger, calendar types, CredentialPayload, getAppKeysFromSlug, parseRefreshTokenResponse). This will fail type-check and throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime whenever a Salesforce credential is used, breaking the Salesforce integration entirely.

findings.title: Defaults missing refresh_token to literal string and persists it
findings.body: When the response has no `refresh_token`, the function sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers spread/save the parsed data back into the credential (e.g. zoomvideo sets `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`; office365calendar spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored key). This overwrites a real refresh token with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, permanently breaking future refreshes. The fallback should preserve the existing stored refresh token, not fabricate one.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, appSlug, userId)` expects a Cal.com user id as its third argument. zoho-bigin passes `credentialId`. When credential sharing is enabled this sends `calcomUserId=<credentialId>` to the self-hoster endpoint, so the wrong user is looked up and the wrong credentials are returned/synced.

findings.title: Sharing-mode returns a raw fetch Response incompatible with most callers' expected shapes
findings.body: In the sharing branch this returns a `fetch` Response whose body (per its own comment) only contains an access token and expiry. Several adapters pass provider-specific parsing over the result and will fail/misbehave in sharing mode: hubspot reads `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` off the raw Response (both undefined → NaN expiry, no access token set); zoho-bigin and zohocrm read `.data.error` (Response has no `.data` → TypeError); lark expects a `RefreshTokenResp` from handleLarkError but gets the minimal body; webex parses with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` which requires literal `scope`/`token_type` that the minimal response lacks → rejection. Only callers that use parseRefreshTokenResponse tolerate the minimal shape.

findings.title: Connection is created with stale access token after refresh
findings.body: getClient always refreshes and writes the new token to the DB, but then constructs the jsforce.Connection with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token`, where `credentialKey` is the pre-refresh credential. The newly obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` is never used, so all API calls use the old (likely expired) token. Additionally getClient now performs a network refresh on every instantiation instead of using the stored token, adding an extra token round-trip per calendar operation.

findings.title: Computed-key schema is broken and does not validate expiry numbers
findings.body: The object literal uses `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as keys. These stringify the Zod schema objects (both evaluate to the same fixed string, e.g. "[object Object]"), so the second definition simply overrides the first and the intended "match any property whose value is a number (the expiry)" behavior never happens. The resulting schema only requires `access_token` and ignores expiry entirely, so the minimum-validity check in sharing mode is silently weaker than documented.

findings.title: Credential-sync request is sent with no authentication
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT includes only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` and no shared secret/authorization, so the self-hoster cannot verify the request actually came from the configured Cal.com instance. Anyone who can reach the endpoint can request credential refreshes for arbitrary user ids/app slugs. It should send an authenticated header derived from a shared secret (analogous to the webhook secret).

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality
findings.body: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` compares the shared secret with `!==`, leaking timing information that can be exploited to recover the secret over many requests. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on Buffers of equal length).

findings.title: No HTTP method check and unhandled zod parse errors
findings.body: The handler never inspects `req.method`, so any verb (GET/PUT/DELETE/...) is accepted as long as the header matches, and `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throwing on an invalid payload surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400. A method guard plus wrapping parse in try/catch (returning 400) would give correct, predictable behavior.
